articles.title: ‘I was nervous before my solo stay in a remote Scottish Highlands cabin – but the solitude is glorious’
articles.summary: As a lone female traveller, the prospect of staying in a hut on Rannoch Moor is daunting, but the silence of the mountains and lochs turns out to be ‘the ultimate luxury’ In the gloaming, the trees stand dark and impenetrable on either side of the path.
body: Just a few minutes earlier, I had been scuffing my feet in the sand by the loch shore, watching as the clouds draped themselves across the top of the Grampians. In the absence of other people, Loch Laidon, silvery in the half-light, had been mine to enjoy; in the woods, however, my solitude feels unnerving.

It is not long before I break out of the trees, following rough boards over boggy moorland to reach the top of the nearest hill. Below, past the green viaduct that carries the West Highland Line, stretches the eastern edge of Rannoch Moor, with layer upon layer of Perthshire’s hills beyond that. Out in the open, my fears dissipate – there is no one here, except for me and the fieldfares that fly squeakily away at my approach.

articles.title: I’m really hurt that my parents didn’t give me a 40th birthday gift | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: You feel overlooked, but your parents’ disappointing behaviour does not necessarily mean they don’t love you. I turned 40 a few years ago. For my 21st and 30th birthdays I got jewellery from my parents, so when they didn’t ask what I wanted, I assumed they would follow this tradition.
body: I place a lot of importance on gift giving. It isn’t about the value, but it’s nice to feel someone has spent time thinking about you. To get nothing just screamed that they didn’t care.

I already have a difficult relationship with my parents because my sister made my childhood a misery. I now refuse to be in her presence. This means my parents have to choose who to spend Christmas with, but even when they want to make it my year, I ’ve often been left feeling I’m the last one to be considered as they’re too busy running round trying to make sure everyone else is happy. I went to stay one year (at their insistence) but on the understanding they would have dinner with my sister. That wasn’t a problem, but they left nothing in the house for me to make my own dinner.

I recently got a new job and moved closer to my parents again, and I’m dreading this year’s holidays. I don’t want to spend them together, but my parents will expect to see me. I don’t think they realise how hurt I still am. How can I navigate this?
points: You feel overlooked, but your parents’ disappointing behaviour does not necessarily mean they don’t love you.
For my 21st and 30th birthdays I got jewellery from my parents, so when they didn’t ask what I wanted, I assumed they would follow this tradition.
It isn’t about the value, but it’s nice to feel someone has spent time thinking about you.
To get nothing just screamed that they didn’t care.

articles.title: ‘Jensen Huang lost his mind’: how AI’s smartest man fell for the world’s oldest trick
articles.summary: Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected spy is Silicon Valley’s worst nightmare come true. The resignation this week of Nvidia’s founder and CEO Jensen Huang is one of the most astonishing corporate scandals in memory, featuring allegations of international espionage and extramarital affairs…
body: Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife of 41 years in a letter to employees this past weekend, following a report from the New York Times that the tech mogul had a close relationship with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China’s government. Huang resigned on Thursday after 33 years as CEO amid reports of two additional affairs with Nvidia employees, causing the world’s most valuable chip company’s stock to plummet.

The scandal has thrown Nvidia into crisis, cast a pall over the AI boom and even threatened the stability of the US economy. Huang’s downfall is a nightmare scenario for a tech industry that has become increasingly fearful of security threats, and a glimpse into what intelligence experts say is a constant theater of corporate espionage secretly playing out every day throughout the US.

“The reason that this is making the news is because obviously you have one of the wealthiest men in the world and one of the highest-profile CEOs in the world,” said Don Aviv, the CEO of corporate intelligence firm Interfor International. “But this happens all the time, across industries.”
points: Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected spy is Silicon Valley’s worst nightmare come true.

articles.title: Why Some Flights Were Exempt From the Ground Stop
articles.summary: Dozens of international flights departed from the United States during Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Some planes also left for Hawaii from the West Coast.
body: Thousands of passengers scrambled to update their travel plans on Saturday as air traffic slowly unsnarled after a nationwide ground stop on Friday, but a number of travelers had already arrived at their destinations on flights left unaffected by the order.

Dozens of international flights took to the skies even as airports across the United States coped with only the third nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration this century. Certain flights were also permitted to depart from the West Coast to Hawaii during the stoppage.
Here’s why some air travel was allowed to proceed even as flight systems were hampered.
More than 8,200 flights were canceled nationwide on Friday — over 31 percent of those scheduled — according to Cirium, an aviation data firm.

articles.title: At 17, I dated a 36-year-old. That decision looks very different to me now | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: As teenagers, my friends and I thought it was glamorous to have relationships with older men. But after the revelations about Russell Brand and David Walliams, I have started to see that period of my life in a new light.
body: I t has been a strange time to be a “woman of a certain age”, as Gregg Wallace so charmingly labelled us. Many of us were consumed by every detail of the Russell Brand trial and the David Walliams exposé. We were pleasantly surprised, albeit dazed – stunned even – by there being consequences for their behaviour, because that’s not how it usually goes, in our experience.

One way to reconcile how so many women’s histories have been altered in the wake of Brand and Walliams is to focus on hope, the positives. On what can change, now that some women, who are far more courageous than I am, have taught all of us how to know better.

articles.title: 44 Best Wedding Guest Dresses in 2026 for Every Type of Ceremony
articles.summary: Shop the best wedding guest dresses for every kind of ceremony and dress code—from a garden wedding to a beach wedding and courthouse ceremony.
body: Once you’ve coordinated your wedding guest schedule, the next step is figuring out what to wear to all those nuptials. Between decoding dress codes (just how casual is a “casual” wedding, really?) and navigating different climates, you’ll quickly realize there’s no one-size-fits-all solution to this sort of occasion styling. So if you find yourself in the run-up to a fancy affair with a closet full of not-quite-right frocks and a looming deadline—don’t panic. We pulled together an edit of the best wedding guest dresses to suit every possible style, venue, and budget.
Whatever’s in the cards (we mean this literally—please read the invite carefully), our picks for the best wedding guest dresses cover a lot of ground.

The coldest days of the year come with the quandary of formal dressing for freezing temps (is there anything worse than having to cover a great dress with a puffer coat?). Stay warm in Staud’s long-sleeve maxi or a velvet option by Veronica Beard. Or, fully embrace winter glam in Simkhai’s halterneck gown, which has a low back for some drama.

articles.title: Walking the Peaks of the Balkans, a Trekking Route With Community At Its Core
articles.summary: The 119-mile inn-to-inn hiking route has reconnected mountain villages in Albania, Kosovo, and Montenegro, once splintered by war—and welcomed the world onto their doorstep.
body: I'm awoken by the sound of cowbells clanging outside my bare-boned wood cabin in Dobërdol, a high mountain settlement in northern Albania. Through the window, slightly fogged from the chilly morning air at 5,700 feet, I see the culprits: five chestnut-colored cows munching on grass just feet from my bedside, their bells and tails swinging away.

I make the short and frigid walk across the guesthouse lawn to the breakfast room, maneuvering around a dozen or so hikers' tents pitched in the grass. Yesterday’s 10-mile trek from Çerem to Dobërdol is still fresh in my mind: dusty dirt trails edged with wild blueberries I couldn’t resist picking and patches of willow gentian, their petals so intensely purple they matched the berry stains on my fingers. The forests of pine, beech, and spruce in these parts are thick enough that the daylight dims inside of them; the valleys dizzyingly deep as they fold in on themselves.
The Peaks of the Balkans trek is a 119-mile inn-to-inn circular trail across the long-disputed borderlands of Albania, Kosovo, and Montenegro.
Local-owned guesthouses welcome trekkers with included meals, like fresh vegetables, homemade dairy, and cured sausages and meats.
points: The 119-mile inn-to-inn hiking route has reconnected mountain villages in Albania, Kosovo, and Montenegro, once splintered by war—and welcomed the world onto their doorstep.

articles.title: All Accounted for After Tanker Crashes Into Docked New Orleans Riverboat
articles.summary: Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana called it a “literal miracle on the Mississippi” that all of the nearly 200 people aboard the riverboat were rescued.
body: A tanker ship struck a riverboat carrying nearly 200 people on Friday in New Orleans, causing the cruise ship to capsize at its dock and prompting a wide-scale search-and-rescue operation, the authorities said.
Mayor Helena Moreno of New Orleans said at a news conference that all passengers of the riverboat, the American Heritage, were accounted for after the crash.
A city of New Orleans spokesperson said on Friday that 32 people were hospitalized. On Saturday the city’s deputy mayor of health and human services said two people had serious injuries.
“It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi,” said Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana, who also spoke at the news conference.
points: Jeff Landry of Louisiana called it a “literal miracle on the Mississippi” that all of the nearly 200 people aboard the riverboat were rescued.

articles.title: 5 Cozy Meals Our Editors Make With Boxed Stuffing
articles.summary: Like one-pan schmaltzy chicken and weeknight pasta with savory crumbs.
body: Each month in Well Stocked, our staff shares unfussy recipe ideas that you can call upon any day of the week. Because yes, our editors love to cook, but sometimes we need to get dinner on the table 12 minutes ago. That’s when we look to pantry and fridge staples that can quickly morph into delicious meals. This month, it’s all about boxed stuffing.

Few Thanksgiving dishes inspire as many strong opinions as stuffing slash dressing. In a baking dish or the bird itself? Sourdough or white bread? Fresh herbs or dried? Sausage or nah? There are the purists, who insist on drying their own bread, chopping aromatics, and seasoning everything from scratch. Then there are the Stove Top loyalists, who grew up on that unmistakable red box and remain fiercely faithful. Site director Rachel Tepper Paley is firmly in the latter camp. “My late father considered boxed Stove Top the Platonic ideal of stuffing, so I grew up with the uber-savory stuff on every Thanksgiving table,” she says. “We continue to serve it every year in his honor.”

articles.title: The Hot List: 20 Must-Have Pieces, According to Instagram’s Favorite Fashion Sourcer
articles.summary: Gab Waller’s monthly cheat sheet of things to shop now before the most dreaded three words in online shopping appear (“out of stock”).
body: November, already!? I’m sure I’m not alone in wondering how we’re possibly already in November. This year has flown by! With Thanksgiving right around the corner, I’m starting to feel the holiday energy and can’t wait for all the festivities over the next two months to close out 2026. As parties fill up calendars, so do my DMs with requests for what to wear to each. I wanted to focus this month’s column on just that. Think velvet, sequins, extra fun colors, embellishments of all kinds, and more. Let the celebrations—and the holiday dressing—begin!
We all collectively need a go-to LBD for the holidays, and this newest style from Khaite ticks all the right boxes. I LOVE that they described it as having a doll-like silhouette. I’ll take it!

Coming in at number one are the party slipper heels from The Row that dominated my DMs. One request came through, followed by a few more, I then posted them on our stories, and as it goes, an instant hit! Now is the time to jump on these.
A snakeskin leather coat!? Say no more! One size is available now, run (or I might need to snap it up for myself!).

articles.title: ‘I Love Being a Girl’: Inside the Life of a Sorority Influencer
articles.summary: Many young adults want to be influencers. And why not? It’s fun. But it also means that the camera is always on.
body: The Alpha Phi sorority house at the University of Arizona occupies a professionally decorated Spanish colonial-style mansion just off campus. There’s a chandeliered dining room, two pink-and-baby-blue living rooms and a tanning area on the roof.

It’s where Haley DeKreek, a 20-year-old junior, lives with her closest friends. It’s also the backdrop to her budding career. Her work takes place mostly in her room, but she picks up the rewards in the mailroom just off the foyer.

Perpetually suffused with floral perfume, it overflows with packages, many of them hers: boxes with dresses for formals or matching yoga sets, boxes of makeup, hair products and skin care. Some she ordered herself, but many are freebies from brands that have spotted her potential as a TikTok influencer, a one-girl campus marketing powerhouse. Nearly all are destined to appear in the many-stepped “get ready with me” videos she has posted since she was a first-year student rushing sororities.
points: But it also means that the camera is always on.

articles.title: What It Took for America to Wipe Out Measles
articles.summary: The U.S. could soon lose its measles elimination status. Winning it was a massive, decades-long undertaking.
body: In March 2000, the nation’s leading measles experts gathered at a Hyatt hotel in Atlanta, just a few miles away from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, to make a historic decision.

After two days of poring over data, they came to a unanimous verdict: Measles, which had infected nearly every American child by age 15 just a few decades earlier, had been eliminated in the United States.

Attendees saw it as a public health milestone, one that the chair of the meeting credited to “millions of parents and children, hundreds of thousands of health workers, and thousands of policymakers and legislators.”

“I walked away with the feeling that this was very monumental,” said Dr. Jonathan Temte, one of the physicians at the meeting. He kept a white binder from the meeting, filled with measles data, as a memento.
points: The U.S. could soon lose its measles elimination status.

articles.title: E.T., Phone Chanel! How Fashion’s Labels Got Personal Again
articles.summary: From Steven Spielberg’s secret Chanel embroidery to love letters, playful logos, and little lambs, fashion is finding new ways to wear its heart on its sleeve—or, rather, inside its lining.
body: E.T., phone home! Or if you’re Steven Spielberg g etting honored at the Museum of Modern Art’s annual Film Benefit, phone Chanel. On Thursday night, Spielberg offered a peek inside his bespoke Chanel tuxedo jacket, courtesy of Matthieu Blazy. Beneath the classic black tailoring was a galaxy-speckled lining, an embroidered playing card featuring E.T. on his bicycle, and a little patch reading “E.T. PHONE HOME.” Spielberg proudly flashed the details for all to see. Now that’s a statement lining.

It’s just the latest in a series of delightfully personal flourishes coming out of Blazy’s Chanel atelier. For his spring 2026 haute couture debut, the designer asked models to contribute something meaningful to their looks: a love letter, a birth date, a lucky symbol, an intimate thought. These were translated into exquisite embroideries by the house’s Lesage atelier, stitched into garments or onto little silk notes tucked inside delicate, translucent Chanel handbags. Model Stephanie Cavalli reportedly chose a letter from her husband. The sentiment was just as beautiful as the craftsmanship.
points: From Steven Spielberg’s secret Chanel embroidery to love letters, playful logos, and little lambs, fashion is finding new ways to wear its heart on its sleeve—or, rather, inside its lining.

articles.title: What a 43-Year-Old Server and Drag Queen Eats on $63 CAN in Toronto, Ontario
articles.summary: Daily Americanos can't help with a stubborn cold, but takeout sushi and a Little Caesars Chicago Deep Dish Meat Treat pizza are good for the soul.
body: Welcome to The Receipt, a series documenting how Bon Appétit readers eat and what they spend doing it. Each food diary follows one anonymous reader’s week of expenses related to groceries, restaurant meals, coffee runs, and every bite in between. In this time of rising food costs, The Receipt reveals how folks—from different cities, with different incomes, on different schedules—are figuring out their food budgets.
In today's Receipt, we follow a 43-year-old server and drag queen in Toronto, Ontario. Keep reading for his receipts.

What is your annual salary, if you have one? Girl, I have no idea. Waiting tables brings in around $60K CAN, and performing in bars, nightclubs and drag brunches probably makes me another $3K, but all those sweat and glitter covered bills get stuffed under a mattress, so who knows?
How much is one paycheck, after taxes? Let’s call it an even thousand dollars.
